The original hanging-mount bug was reportedly fixed separately with mount namespaces, so it is unclear whether removing the fuseblk default is the right fix.

The regression potential is factually wrong. os-prober is not simply disabled by default, because it is automatically enabled when other OSes are detected at install time. The description admits the change stops os-prober from searching any filesystem that grub-probe does not recognise, which could hide legitimate OS installs. This risk has not been quantified or tested, and the test plan covers only the LVM snapshot case, with no check that non-snapshot unknown filesystems still behave acceptably.

The Other info section says the fix should also be backported to Noble and Jammy, but the SRU does not state which series it targets. The test plan also does not describe the verification steps for each affected release.

The fix landed in tenacious (and a stonking debdiff exists), but the affected release, resolute, has no upload. The reporter says the 1.9.1-0.1ubuntu4 build cannot be installed on 26.04 because it links libcrypto.so.4. The SRU needs a resolute-targeted build.

It also gives no root-cause link for the 3.0.14 regression, so it is unclear whether Noble or Jammy need changes. Whether the stonking upload is needed at all is also unresolved, since the second patch is effectively a no-op there.
No PPA test build has been linked, so reviewers and affected users cannot test the patched packages. Real-hardware verification is only anecdotal and was done by manual patching.
The patches are not in d/p/series in upstream order, although upstream commit 6bde508 depends on 5894be2. The short commit hashes in the patch URLs should also be full hashes.

Usually for devel release patch, we have to add the fields in the commit message:

There are two standing issues with these patches:
